name: COUNT
description: COUNT counts the number of cells that contain numbers within a specified range.
tldr: COUNT returns the count of cells containing numbers in a range.

parameters.name: value1
parameters.description: The first item, cell reference, or range to count.

parameters.name: value2
parameters.description: Optional additional items, cell references, or ranges to count.

basicExample.description: Count the number of numeric entries in a range
basicExample.explanation: Counts how many cells in A1:A10 contain numbers, ignoring text and blank cells.

advancedExamples.title: Count across multiple ranges
advancedExamples.description: Count numeric values across multiple non-contiguous ranges
advancedExamples.explanation: Counts numbers in three separate columns and returns the total.

advancedExamples.title: Count with criteria using COUNTIF
advancedExamples.description: For conditional counting, use COUNTIF or COUNTIFS instead
advancedExamples.explanation: COUNTIF counts cells that meet a specific condition, like values greater than 50.

howItWorks: COUNT scans each cell in the specified range and counts only those containing numeric values. It ignores empty cells, text, logical values (TRUE/FALSE), and error values.

howToSteps.name: Select a cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where you want the count result to appear.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =COUNT(range) where range is your data.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the number of numeric cells.

limitations: COUNT only counts cells with numeric values — text, blanks, and logical values are ignored.
Use COUNTA to count all non-empty cells, or COUNTIF/COUNTIFS for conditional counting.

commonErrors.cause: No numeric values found in the range
commonErrors.fix: Check your data range or use COUNTA if you want to count all non-empty cells.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: COUNT works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax.

faq.question: What is the difference between COUNT and COUNTA?
faq.answer: COUNT only counts numeric values, while COUNTA counts all non-empty cells including text and logical values.

faq.question: Does COUNT include blank cells?
faq.answer: No, COUNT ignores blank cells. Use COUNTA or COUNTBLANK to count blanks.

faq.question: Can COUNT count across multiple sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, you can reference ranges from multiple sheets: =COUNT(Sheet1!A1:A10, Sheet2!A1:A10)
